places.name: Experimentarium
places.description: 6-year-old runs bubble labs, water tables and physics stations across three interactive floors, plus a dedicated Miniverse zone. 1-year-old crawls freely on soft carpeted floors in the Miniverse, a play space built for ages 1-5 with a nursery room and pram parking.
places.baby_notes: Miniverse has a nursery room, stroller parking and carpeted floor for crawling and first steps.
places.tips: Arrive at opening to get a locker and stroller-parking spot in Miniverse before it fills up.

places.name: National Museum of Denmark (Nationalmuseet)
places.description: 6-year-old explores the ground-floor Children's Museum, an indoor playground for dressing up, a Viking ship replica and hands-on history displays. 1-year-old can crawl on carpeted play areas in the Children's Museum while parents take turns with a museum-provided pram.
places.baby_notes: Own prams stay at the entrance; the museum lends loan prams, and the Children's Museum floor is safe for crawling and cruising.
places.tips: Leave your own pram at the info desk and borrow one of the museum's — own prams aren't allowed into exhibition rooms.

places.name: Tycho Brahe Planetarium
places.description: 6-year-old watches an IMAX-style dome film on a 1,000 sq m tilted screen, picking an English-language showtime. 1-year-old can sit on a parent's lap in the reclined dome seating for a short, dark, low-stimulation break from the rain.
places.baby_notes: No floor space to crawl — babies stay on a lap in the dome seating for one film.
places.tips: Book an English-language show in advance — many screenings are Danish-only.

places.name: BLOX / Danish Architecture Center
places.description: 6-year-old builds with a huge table of Lego bricks next to Lego models of famous Danish buildings, then explores changing architecture exhibitions. 1-year-old can cruise around the open, flat exhibition floors and the ground-floor public atrium.
places.baby_notes: Open, flat exhibition floors and a ground-floor atrium give a baby room to crawl and cruise out of the rain.
places.tips: Kids under 18 enter free with a paying adult — check the ground-floor Lego table isn't fully booked by a school group.

places.name: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark
places.description: 6-year-old joins the Children's Workshop on weekends and holidays to paint, work with clay and plaster alongside resident artists. 1-year-old can crawl in the wide, flat sculpture halls and garden hall, out of the weather.
places.baby_notes: Wide flat gallery halls give a baby space to crawl; the Children's Workshop only runs weekends and school holidays.
places.tips: The Children's Workshop is included in (free) admission but only open Sat-Sun and holiday periods — check it's running on your visit day.

places.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.description: 6-year-old wanders Roman and Egyptian sculpture halls and the palm-filled Winter Garden with a fountain. 1-year-old can be walked or crawl on the flat stone floor of the Winter Garden while adults linger over the antiquities.
places.baby_notes: The Winter Garden's flat stone floor and open space under a glass roof suit a cruising or crawling baby.
places.tips: Free entry on the last Wednesday of the month, but expect it busier then.

places.name: Copenhagen Zoo
places.description: 6-year-old tracks down elephants, lions and the Arctic Ring polar bears across wide outdoor paths built for exploring. 1-year-old naps in the pram between stops or crawls on grass near the children's zoo petting area.
places.baby_notes: Grassy children's zoo area lets a walking 1-year-old crawl safely; several indoor houses give shade and nappy-change breaks.
places.tips: Arrive at opening to beat tour-bus crowds and get feeding-time slots.

places.name: Frederiksberg Have
places.description: 6-year-old runs the winding paths, spots the canal boats and free-roaming birds, and climbs at the playground. 1-year-old crawls on open lawns or naps in pram shade under old trees.
places.baby_notes: Wide grass lawns near the playground area are flat and safe for early walking.
places.tips: Combine with the adjacent zoo visit, entrance right next door.

places.name: Botanical Garden (Botanisk Have)
places.description: 6-year-old hunts for giant leaves, ponds with ducks, and the old Palm House glasshouse. 1-year-old crawls on lawns near the entrance or dozes in the pram along shaded gravel paths.
places.baby_notes: Lawns near the pond are calm and flat; Palm House gives indoor shelter if it rains later.
places.tips: Palm House charges separate small entry fee; garden itself is free.

places.name: Fælledparken Tower Playground (Tårnlegepladsen)
places.description: 6-year-old climbs and slides down miniature versions of Copenhagen's famous towers and free-rents a balance bike during staffed hours. 1-year-old crawls on the soft rubber and sand surfacing at the toddler end.
places.baby_notes: Sand and rubber-matted toddler zone away from the taller tower structures suits a new walker.
places.tips: Free bike/trike loan runs only during staffed hours, check on arrival.

places.name: Kastellet
places.description: 6-year-old runs the star-shaped ramparts, spots the windmill and cannons, and looks for the moat swans. 1-year-old crawls on the flat grass bastions or naps in the pram on the ring-road paths.
places.baby_notes: Flat grass ramparts atop the fortress walls are open and safe for early crawling/walking.
places.tips: Combine with a walk to The Little Mermaid statue nearby.

places.name: Broens Gadekøkken
places.description: 6-year-old picks from dozens of stalls (pizza, noodles, burgers) at a harbour-view picnic table. 1-year-old sits in a high chair by the water's edge, watching boats and harbour buses go by.
places.baby_notes: Communal harbourside tables have open floor space for a pram parked right beside high chairs.
places.tips: Seasonal (spring-autumn only), arrive before noon to grab a shaded harbourside table.

places.name: Bermuda Triangle Playground, Nørrebroparken
places.description: The 6-year-old climbs the crashed-plane and shipwreck structures, ziplines and sandpits in the main park. The 1-year-old crawls safely in the playground's separate toddler zone, away from the bigger climbing frames, with a baby-changing room and bottle-warming microwave right beside it.
places.baby_notes: Dedicated toddler zone fenced off from the bigger structures, plus a staffed indoor activity house nearby for shelter.
places.tips: Staffed Mon-Thu 9:30-17:00, Fri 10:00-17:30; open but unstaffed weekends.

places.name: Toddler Playground at Christianshavns Vold (Panterens Bastion)
places.description: The 6-year-old can walk over to the larger staffed playground a short stroll away on the same ramparts for bigger equipment, while the 1-year-old crawls in this small, toddler-only playground with a big sandbox, seesaw and rocking animals, well away from older kids. The grassy rampart setting is calm and easy to supervise.
places.baby_notes: Small sandbox with seesaw and rocking animals sized for toddlers only, separate from the larger staffed playground on the same rampart.
places.tips: Combine with a walk along the grassy ramparts; bring your own snacks as there's no kiosk on site.

places.name: Trafiklegepladsen i Fælledparken (Traffic Playground)
places.description: The 6-year-old pedals go-karts and bikes around a mini traffic city with real road signs, roundabouts and cycle paths. The 1-year-old has a separate baby-and-toddler section with its own slides, away from the older kids' traffic circuit, plus a Tuesday-morning baby playroom with bottle-warming facilities.
places.baby_notes: Separate toddler and baby section with its own slides, distinct from the older kids' traffic-circuit area; Tuesday 10am baby playroom (0-2 years) with a kitchen for heating bottles.
places.tips: Staffed Mon-Fri 9-17 and weekends 10-17 in even weeks (summer season); go-karts are the big draw for 6-year-olds.

places.name: The King's Garden Playground (Kongens Have)
places.description: The 6-year-old rides the giant bronze dragon and explores the golden-egg island reached over a sand-filled moat. The 1-year-old can crawl safely on the enclosed grass since the whole playground is fenced with hedges and has just one entrance, so a toddler can't wander into traffic or away from the group even with older children around.
places.baby_notes: Fully hedge-enclosed with a single entrance, so a crawling baby is contained even without a formally separate zone; grass is soft for sitting and crawling.
places.tips: Pair with an ice cream from the on-site kiosk; garden paths are stroller- and wheelchair-friendly throughout.

places.name: Restaurant Tight
places.description: Housed in an 1800s building near Strøget, large parts of the menu are marked GF including a kids burger the 6-year-old can order themselves. The 1-year-old rides in a high chair at the table while adults work through the a la carte lunch.
places.tips: Book lunch sitting, calmer with a stroller than dinner service.

places.name: Gorm's Magstræde
places.description: Thin-crust pizza with a fully gluten-free dough option across the whole menu, cooked separately from regular pans. The 6-year-old picks a kids-size pizza while the 1-year-old sits in a high chair between the wood-panelled booths.
places.tips: Mention gluten-free celiac-level care isn't guaranteed — pans are separate but same oven, so ask staff about cross-contact if severe.

places.name: Wagamama Tivoli
places.description: Long communal benches inside Tivoli Gardens serving noodles, ramen and rice bowls, with gluten-free noodles and tofu dishes available on request. The 6-year-old gets their own kids menu while the 1-year-old sits in a high chair, handy for a lunch break between Tivoli rides.
places.tips: Ask staff for the allergen-marked menu — no dedicated GF menu, but noodles/pad thai/tofu are swappable.

places.name: H.U.G Bageri
places.description: Fully gluten-free organic bakery near the lakes, so every pastry on the shelf is safe for a gluten-free 6-year-old to pick themselves without asking. Buggy fits inside for the 1-year-old, ideal for a nap-and-snack stop after the lakes path.
places.tips: Small shop — go off-peak (mid-morning weekday) with a pram.
